Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

basis noun

what something rests on, its grounds

also foundation, grounds, on the basis of, based on, be based on, rest on

classical

Cic. Planc. 29: pietās fundāmentum est omnium virtūtum
Cic. Off. 1.23: fundāmentum autem est jūstitiae fidēs

fundāmentum, fundāmentī n.

noun, second declension

the foundation, the basis (of a virtue, an argument, a life)

Of buildings usually plural (see foundations); of virtues, arguments and plans in either number: jacere pācis fundāmenta, to lay the basis of peace (Cic. Phil. 1.1, Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • mementōte eam mē senectūtem laudāre, quae fundāmentīs adulēscentiae cōnstitūta sit

    remember that the old age I praise is one built on the foundations laid in youthCic. Sen. 62

  • pietās fundāmentum est omnium virtūtum

    dutiful love is the basis of all the virtuesCic. Planc. 29

  • Jam teneō. Ex verbīs tuīs colligō tē pecūniam magis quam cōnsilium ā mē petere.

    Now I get it. I gather from what you say that you are asking me for money rather than advice.Traupman 92

Other words

  • nītor, nītī, nīsus sum — rest on, be based on, rely on

    verb, third conjugation, deponent; with in and the ablative, or the ablative alone · also used · classical · Cic. Div. 2.55: conjectūra omnis, in quā nītitur dīvīnātiō; Cic. Off. 1.122: quōrum cōnsiliō atque auctōritāte nītātur

    “X is based on Y”: X in Y nītitur. Lewis & Short: “to rest, rely, depend upon a thing”.

  • ex (+ ablative) — on the basis of, according to, from

    preposition, with the ablative · also used · classical · Traupman 92: Ex verbīs tuīs colligō, I infer from what you say

    What a conclusion or a claim rests on: ex tuīs litterīs, on the strength of your letter.

See also foundations, base, reason.

SourcesLewis & Short: fundamentum · Lewis & Short: nitor · Lewis & Short: ex
